2026-11-16.patch_summary: This patch series addresses four issues related to Transparent Huge Pages (THP) migration, PTE swap-in, and device-private smaps in the Linux kernel. The first fix prevents a folio reference leak during THP splitting. The second patch avoids mapping hardware-poisoned pages of large anonymous swap-cache folios during PTE swap-in batching. The third change stops reading accessed and dirty bits from non-present PMDs in smaps, where they represent softleaf entries rather than actual state. Finally, the fourth patch accounts for device-private PMDs using mapcounts in smaps, ensuring shared mappings receive proportional Page-Sharing (PSS) and exclusive mappings are counted as private.

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta)
reviews.summary: Reviewer Kiryl noted that memory_failure() cannot split a large file folio, leaving the poisoned page in it, and suggested adding a check to handle this case by setting needs_fallback = true when a poisoned page is found.
reviews.raw_body:
With the check moved up as David and Zi suggested:

Reviewed-by: Kiryl Shutsemau (Meta) <kas@kernel.org>

Do we have the same problem on the file side?

If memory_failure() cannot split a large file folio, it stays in the
page cache with the poisoned page in it.

Consider a write fault through MAP_SHARED on a good page of that folio:

  do_shared_fault()
    __do_fault()
      PageHWPoison(vmf->page)
        // checks the faulting page only
    finish_fault()
      do_set_pmd()
        folio_test_has_hwpoisoned(folio)
          // backs off with VM_FAULT_FALLBACK
      set_pte_range(vmf, folio, &folio->page, folio_nr_pages(folio), addr)
        // maps the poisoned page as well

Possible fix is below. I can post a proper patch if the analysis looks
correct.

diff --git a/mm/memory.c b/mm/memory.c
index fb76d8922e37..25b53847943f 100644
--- a/mm/memory.c
+++ b/mm/memory.c
@@ -5893,6 +5893,10 @@ vm_fault_t finish_fault(struct vm_fault *vmf)
 			return ret;
 	}
 
+	/* A poisoned page must take its own fault */
+	if (folio_contain_hwpoisoned_page(folio))
+		needs_fallback = true;
+
 	if (!needs_fallback && vma->vm_file) {
 		struct address_space *mapping = vma->vm_file->f_mapping;
 		pgoff_t file_end;
-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov

reviews.author: Kiryl (Meta)
reviews.summary: Reviewer Kiryl noted that smaps_pmd_entry() dereferences pmd six times, suggesting a separate patch to read it once with pmdp_get() before this one, and moving pmd_young() and pmd_dirty() under the present branch.
reviews.raw_body:
smaps_pmd_entry() dereferences pmd six times :/

Could you read it once with pmdp_get() in a separate patch before this
one, the way smaps_pte_entry() does with ptep_get()?

This patch would then only move pmd_young() and pmd_dirty() under the
present branch.

-- 
  Kiryl Shutsemau / Kirill A. Shutemov
